confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from five web searches. The RBA search returned the 18 Nov 2026 observation. The other searches returned Numbeo's Matsuyama page (updated Jan 2026, crowdsourced, wide ranges), Livingcost.org and Nomad.watch, and scattered restaurant listings. Inexpensive meal (about ¥1,000) and mid-range dinner for two (about ¥5,000) agree across sources. I converted yen to USD at an assumed rate of roughly ¥150-155 per USD, which I did not look up, so USD figures could be off by several percent. Numbeo's draft beer (about ¥326) and cappuccino (about ¥370) look low for a restaurant or cafe, so I adjusted them upward using Livingcost's pub-beer and cappuccino figures and general knowledge of Japanese menu prices. I found no direct aggregated cocktail or wine price. A single Matsuyama menu showed a glass of wine at ¥770. The cocktail estimate is based on the usual Japanese relationship to beer, with a cocktail at roughly 1.4-1.6 times a beer, and wine at roughly 1.3-1.4 times a beer. All four accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge of Japanese regional-city hostel and business-hotel pricing. I did not search accommodation prices or inspect any listings. They are the least certain anchors, especially for July 2026 demand swings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Matsuyama is a mid-sized regional Japanese city (Shikoku) with a tourism draw from Dogo Onsen and Matsuyama Castle. Prices are comparable to other regional Japanese cities such as Okayama or Hiroshima, and are below Tokyo, Kyoto and Osaka. Accommodation reflects typical business-hotel and small-guesthouse pricing outside the major metros.
